newsitem.title: POLAND: NFI units jump 5.9 pct in soaring trade.
newsitem.headline: NFI units jump 5.9 pct in soaring trade.

text.p: Polish mass privatisation NFI units jumped 5.9 percent to 125 zlotys in record 57.9-million zloty turnover on Wednesday, soaring 43.7 percent since late August, and are likely to keep rising, traders said.

They said the current surge might be caused by large investors buying the units in expectation of good financial data of the more than 500 companies held by National Investment Funds (NFIs) to be released over the next two months.
"Investors think the financial results of the companies might be good, so the units are surging," one trader said.
But some traders said the NFI surge might be caused by domestic speculators keen to take profits, with some traders expecting a correction early next week.
Analysts said it was as yet impossible to appraise the units sufficiently and that the presentation of firms' financial data would give investors a better clue.
The units started bourse trade on July 15 at 104 zlotys.

They have been on offer to Poland's 28 million adults since November at 20 zlotys per unit and will later be exchangeable for shares in each of the country's 15 National Investment Funds, grouping more than 500 firms undergoing privatisation.
So far more than 17.7 million NFI units have been sold on the primary market, with the certificates on offer until November 21 this year.
